summary: St. Lawrence County lookout south of Cranberry Lake: 1910 37-ft tower, 1917 47-ft steel tower; listed as gone, with no removal date or site description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no removal date or site description in the sources read
facts.agency: Forest, Fish and Game Commission, then Conservation Commission

events.note: State fire superintendents decided to add a lookout at Cat Mountain, south of Cranberry Lake
A lookout was established atop a 37-foot tower at a cost of $698.96
A 47-foot steel tower was erected; the source does not say whether it replaced the 1910 tower
Ed Akey of Kanakena was expected back on Cat Mountain
Harry E. Watson, a fire ranger at the Cat Mountain tower, died; he had been a fire observer at Cranberry Lake for eleven years

corrections.why: The brief's 11.3 m (37 ft) is the 1910 tower. The same page reports a 47-foot steel tower erected by 1917. The sources do not say which tower stood when it was removed, so this is a low-confidence correction.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, and the main one is a compilation of newspaper clippings and annual-report citations that we did not open. Searches for a Cat Mountain tower near Cranberry Lake found only Cathead Mountain (near Benson, Hamilton County) and Catamount Mountain (near South Colton, St. Lawrence County), which are different peaks, so they are not used. No source gives a removal date or describes the site today. Two WebSearch calls were used for this lookout.
